Tue, September 1, 2026 at 6:12 PM UTC Bex Evans

Software stocks crushed chips in August. History says September gets tougher. Software's second-best month since 2002, paired with a reversal in chip and AI infrastructure stocks, made for a record divergence between software and chip stocks in August. What comes next might not be so rosy for software.
Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre reports:
That leaves September with a very different starting point. Software enters the month with the momentum, while much of the physical AI trade is already on the defensive.
And this wasn't an ordinary software rally.
A broader S&P software index gained roughly 14% in August, its strongest August in data going back to 1990.
So Yahoo Finance looked at the 12 strongest prior August rallies in software over that history and what happened next.
Software historically held up through Sept. 15, with a median gain of about 1%. Semiconductors were already down roughly 1% by then.
Then things got tougher.
From Sept. 15 through month-end, median software returns fell roughly 1%, the S&P 500 dropped almost 2%, and semiconductors slid about 3.5%.
Twelve observations make a small sample, so this is a tendency rather than a forecast.
The broader calendar isn't particularly friendly either. September has historically been the weakest month for the S&P 500, while volatility has tended to pick up as summer ends .
August showed the market could rotate around weak chips. September will show how long that can last.

New Apple CEO John Ternus logs on New Apple ( AAPL ) CEO John Ternus has officially signed on.
"Hello," he simply wrote in his first post on X, greeting over 66K followers. Apple investors appeared enthused, with the stock rising 3% in afternoon trading.

"Congrats!" SpaceX CEO Elon Musk replied, chief executive to chief executive.
As my colleague Dan Howley has reported, Ternus will need to get to work quickly.
Apple is set to host its annual iPhone event in early September, where it's expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone. There's also a lot of scrutiny on what Apple's AI-powered Siri will look like.
Like Tim Cook before him, Ternus will need to become a master diplomat, navigating Apple's relationship with the Trump administration and changing regulatory landscape for the App Store.
Plus, Apple is currently embroiled in a heated legal battle with OpenAI over its trade secrets and hardware competition.
Cook will continue to serve as an executive chairman, and he may help advise on some of these issues. But after a settling-in period, it will be up to Ternus to make the next era of Apple his own.

Musk predicts AI will grow the global economy 'by 20% to 30%' Tesla ( TSLA ) and SpaceX ( SPCX ) CEO Elon Musk rarely shies away from making bold predictions about new technologies. His comments at the G20 summit for central bankers and finance ministers were no different.
"We are going to see and are seeing, in fact, significant productivity gains from artificial intelligence, and we'll see very dramatic gains in productivity from robotics," Musk said, appearing virtually at the summit in Asheville, N.C.
"Just to give you some sense of scale here, I think AI will probably increase the global economy by 20% to 30%," Musk added. "That's my rough estimate, meaning on the order of $20 trillion to $30 trillion per year."
Musk advocated for regulators to encourage and embrace new technology like AI, arguing that it should be "default legal" rather than "default illegal."
He was most bullish on robotics, predicting that there would be a billion humanoid robots in the next decade.
"AI will be able to do anything digital, anything that does not require shaping of atoms by hand, probably by the end of next year."

The OpenAI-Apple battle is escalating, 2 new legal filings show OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) fought back against allegations that it stole trade secrets from Apple ( AAPL ), according to a new court filing published on Monday, as a legal battle between the two highly secretive tech firms heats up.
"This dispute is a mess of Apple's own making, and it is trying to blame everyone else," OpenAI said in the filing. "Apple blames employees who left the company for taking their personal accounts with them — even though Apple encouraged them to use personal accounts for work."
Apple alleges that two OpenAI employees, Tang Tan and Chang Liu, who formerly worked at Apple, gave Apple's proprietary information to OpenAI.
In a separate filing on Monday, Apple also accused OpenAI of destroying evidence , Bloomberg reported.
OpenAI called Apple's lawsuit "baseless," blaming the iPhone maker's own "sloppy" offboarding processes for its complaints and arguing that Apple was attempting to delay OpenAI's competing hardware device.
At the heart of the case is a growing rivalry between the companies as they move to build devices that can dominate in the AI age. OpenAI's device for ChatGPT "differs materially from known Apple products," the startup said, but it poses a risk to eroding the market share of the iPhone.

Amazon stock drops on report of planned FTC lawsuit Amazon ( AMZN ) stock tumbled about 3% on Monday after a Wall Street Journal report said the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) plans to sue the e-commerce giant, accusing it of manipulating the prices businesses paid for advertising on its retail platform.
The suit, which includes a coalition of more than 20 state attorneys general, is expected to state that Amazon misled advertisers by covertly increasing the minimum amount they were required to pay to have their products' ads featured, according to FTC officials.
The lawsuit is expected to claim that the price manipulation practice generated tens of billions of dollars in profit for the company over seven years.

Mon, August 31, 2026 at 5:31 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Tim Cook shares farewell message on last day as Apple CEO Apple CEO Tim Cook sent a message to Apple employees, investors, and fans as he makes his exit from the top role at the iPhone maker today.
Cook, who will continue to serve as executive chairman at Apple, while John Ternus takes over the CEO position, evoked the visionary ethos of Apple's founder Steve Jobs as he urged employees to "leave our 'dent in the universe.'"
"We have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it," Cook wrote in a heartfelt message. "That purpose is part of what makes this place extraordinary."
Cook also shared a message of overwhelming gratitude on X.
"Sending lots of love to the Apple community on my last day as CEO," Cook said. "My title changes tomorrow, but the love I have for the Apple community never will. Thank you for being a constant source of inspiration. My gratitude is endless, and I'm excited for the next chapter!"
Read more about what Cook said in his memo to employees here.

Mon, August 31, 2026 at 4:07 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

'Let Data Reign': Trump champions data center build-out amid growing backlash President Trump threw his support behind the data center build-out on Monday, framing the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence as a matter of economic and national security.
"The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor," Trump said in a social media post. "If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign."
Trump called the US's artificial intelligence lead "the Golden Goose" that every country wants. "China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement," Trump added.

Trump seemed to appeal directly to the communities that could block Big Tech's ambitions, as a swiftly growing backlash against building data centers has taken hold in the US and states have begun issuing moratoriums to slow new construction.
That has led some strategists to note that the biggest bottleneck in the AI build-out may not be securing enough high-powered chips or energy to run the data centers. It could be the public's permission.
In the lead-up to the midterm elections, the politics of data centers has grown thornier as supporters point to AI as the next engine of economic growth, while critics raise concerns about rising energy bills and a general mistrust of Silicon Valley.

Mon, August 31, 2026 at 3:27 PM UTC Jake Conley

Nvidia will invest $3.5 billion in Taiwanese chipmaker MediaTek, companies say Monday Nvidia ( NVDA ) has agreed to invest $3.5 billion in Taiwanese chipmaker MediaTek, per a statement Monday morning, deepening Nvidia's already large web of investments throughout the AI ecosystem.
"NVIDIA and MediaTek today announced a deepening of their longstanding collaboration to build the next generations of AI computing platforms — spanning AI infrastructure, local AI computing and automotive," the companies said in a joint statement, noting the combination will combine Nvidia's computing platforms with MediaTek's chip design capabilities.
Shares in Nvidia trended up by roughly 1% on Monday morning.

The deal is set to broaden an existing partnership between the two AI companies. Under this round of investment, MediaTek will use Nvidia's NVLink Fusion technology, among other applications, which functions as connective tissue that allows customers to plug their own chips into Nvidia's underlying data center architecture.
NVLink Fusion will allow MediaTek to "provide hyperscalers, cloud service providers and frontier model developers with a prevalidated path to develop custom XPUs and bring them into NVIDIA NVLink™-connected, rack-scale AI factories," the companies said in their statement.
The investment from Nvidia — adding to billions of dollars Jensen Huang's company has invested in companies throughout the AI ecosystem — comes as Nvidia increasingly focuses on positioning its technology as the base architecture for the AI build-out, moving toward a place where the entire AI ecosystem runs on Nvidia's systems.
"The part that people don't see about our growth because we're practically singular because of the nature of how we deliver products. I mean we're the only company in the world that creates and builds, offers an entire AI factory platform, a full-stack system," Huang said on the company's second quarter earnings call.

SpaceX stock in focus as OpenAI ends Cursor access to AI models SpaceX ( SPCX ) stock is in focus on Monday after big news over the weekend concerning its AI coding tool Cursor and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ).

items.body:
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el jueves que pedirá a los países europeos que reembolsen a Estados Unidos la ayuda militar y las municiones enviadas previamente a Ucrania, y pareció insinuar que se suspenderían las ventas a los países aliados.
En una publicación en las redes sociales, Trump también criticó duramente los informes que apuntan a que las reservas de munición de Estados Unidos se habían reducido considerablemente debido a la guerra en Irán, al tiempo que añadió que el país está acumulando munición.
"Las estamos reservando para nosotros, EEUU, en lugar de venderlas a otros, pero las ventas a los aliados se reanudarán pronto", escribió Trump.
"Se entregaron cientos de miles de millones de dólares a Ucrania y a la OTAN, de forma gratuita, que Europa habría pagado —si se les hubiera pedido—, ¡pero vamos a pedir ese dinero, aunque sea con algo de retraso!", añadió.
Reuters informó el mes pasado de que el Ejército estadounidense ha agotado gran parte de sus reservas de misiles de largo alcance de alta precisión durante la guerra con Irán, lo que ha suscitado preocupación sobre la preparación de las Fuerzas Armadas para futuros conflictos.

items.title: Canada July trade surplus shrinks, weeks before new U.S. tariffs
items.author: Reuters Staff
items.summary: Canada’s trade surplus sharply narrowed in July as exports of energy and metal products shrank while imports rose, data showed on Thursday, just weeks before a major escalation in trade dispute with ...
items.body: OTTAWA — Canada’s trade surplus narrowed sharply in July as exports of energy and metal products shrank while imports rose, just weeks before Washington’s new 50 per cent tariffs begin to show up in statistics, posing a stiffer test for Canadian exporters. The trade surplus was $769 million, compared with a four-year high surplus of $4.2 billion posted a month ago, Statistics Canada said on Thursday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a surplus of $3.57 billion in July. Exports dropped 2.3 per cent, while imports increased 2.2 per cent. Amid an escalating trade dispute with U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration, Canada has been seeking to reduce its dependence on its neighbor and largest trading partner. The U.S. accounted for 66.35 per cent of Canada’s total exports in July, down from 69.39 per cent in June and 72.64 per cent a year ago. However, Canada’s import dependence on the U.S. has only narrowed to 59 per cent in the last 12 months compared with 62 per cent in 2024. The July figures, Canada’s fifth consecutive monthly trade surplus, extended a run of relatively resilient Canadian trade despite more than a year and a half of U.S. tariffs. However, Washington’s latest duties, imposed last month, will provide a tougher test for exporters in the coming months. The decrease in exports in July was primarily led by energy products, which account for almost a quarter of Canada’s total exports, and 95 per cent of which usually flow south of the border. Their value dropped 4.4 per cent in July, a third consecutive monthly decline after exports of crude oil decreased by 5.5 per cent, with both prices and volumes falling, StatsCan said. Exports of metal and non-metallic mineral products, which posted an increase of 15.8 per cent in the prior month, also shrank by 8.5 per cent in July. As a result, Canada’s total exports fell to $76.14 billion, down from $77.96 billion in June, but excluding metals and energy, exports increased 0.6 per cent in July. The overall decrease in total exports in July was partially offset by higher exports of aircraft and other transportation equipment and parts, which surged by 34.9 per cent. Imports rose in July to a value of $75.37 billion, up from $73.76 billion, StatsCan said, adding that it was the sixth consecutive monthly increase. This was led by an 11.4 per cent increase in imports of motor vehicles and parts, mainly from the U.S. Exports to the U.S. dropped 6.6 per cent in July while imports from the country increased by 1.8 per cent, shrinking Canada’s trade surplus with its main trading partner by more than 40 per cent to $5.9 billion. Stuart Bergman, chief economist at Export Development Canada, the country’s official export credit agency, said that keeping the share of Canada’s exports going to the U.S. below 70 per cent was an encouraging trend. “Sheer gravity alone pulls exporters to the U.S. market,” Bergman said, but added that there have been concerted efforts to shift some of that gravity to other markets, citing the increase in agricultural exports, especially canola to China and Japan. Year-to-date share of exports to the U.S. is around 68 per cent, down from 73 per cent in the year-ago period. Exports to countries other than the United States rose 7.4 per cent, while imports increased 2.8 per cent, leaving Canada with a non-U.S. trade deficit of $5.1 billion, down from $6.1 billion in the prior month. The Canadian dollar was trading firmer, up 0.35 per cent to $1.3792 against the U.S. dollar, or 72.51 U.S. cents. --- Reporting by Promit Mukherjee; Editing by Dale Smith; Editing by Sharon Singleton

items.title: Is the world worried about the wrong debt?
items.author: Balazs Koranyi
items.creator: Balazs Koranyi
items.summary: Hi there. Carmel is away this week, so I’m filling in for her and wanted to discuss a debt issue that may be flying under the radar for some.
items.body:
Hi there. Carmel is away this week, so I’m filling in for her and wanted to discuss a debt issue that may be flying under the radar for some.
All the market talk has been [USN:L4N44S076 TEXT:"focused on U.S. debt"] hitting $40 trillion this summer, with interest costs rising to over $1 trillion a year as the 10-year yield inches towards 5%. Sure, the U.S. is on an unsustainable path and the [USN:FWN44G0QP TEXT:"Treasury’s efforts to bring down"] longer-term borrowing costs are likely to prove futile without meaningful fiscal correction. But the U.S. enjoys the exorbitant privilege of issuing the world’s reserve currency in the deepest bond market. Capital keeps flowing in and economic growth remains stellar, driven by massive AI investments. So its debt market may be creaking, but it’s certainly not breaking just yet.
France, the euro zone’s second-biggest economy, may be in a far more precarious position, however.
At 117% of GDP, it has one of the highest debt levels in the developed world and is heading into a tense presidential election in which the frontrunners are [USN:L8N44I0JF TEXT:"hard-left and far-right candidates"] both pushing expensive platforms. And French governments already have a long history of retreating from reforms in the face of street protests and political pressure.
This lack of economic transformation has left growth below 1%, which makes it essentially impossible for the country to grow out of its debt. Spending meanwhile remains unsustainably high and the [USN:L8N44H1DA TEXT:"budget deficit"] will again exceed the target this year. Reflecting those troubles, the 10-year French yield, a key gauge of perceived financial health, has risen to around 4.25% this summer, almost double the central bank interest rate.
The regional implications of any capital flight could be massive. Italy, Spain and Belgium all have debt levels in excess of 100% of GDP, so the risk of contagion and turbulence is high. That would then put pressure on the only entity that could restore calm to the euro zone bond market: the European Central Bank.
The ECB has the firepower to calm markets but has so far gone out of its way not to use it. It has spent years reducing its government bond holdings and set tough conditions for any market intervention. Its Transmission Protection Instrument could be used to hoover up debt and push yields back down, but only in case of “unwarranted” market moves.
It is hard to argue that a rise in yields for an indebted country with weak economic fundamentals amid political turmoil is not warranted. France is too big to fail, however, and the ECB could come under pressure to intervene, even if the legal justifications could be questionable.
The spread between 10-year German and French debt, a key indicator of investors’ risk appetite, has been inching up all summer and stands at 87 basis points, above that for Italy and its highest level in years. While it is not yet in the danger zone, it’s clearly moving in the wrong direction, and it may be just a matter of time before the ECB’s resolve is tested again.

THE PODCAST ""Left behind regions: regions that are experiencing youth out-migration, they're experiencing less economic growth in comparison to more urban capitals that are doing really well... the tax base is also reducing, so public services are also going to be reduced... many people living there have the sentiment that they're losing in the social contract, they're losing in this transition. What happened: Broadcom ( AVGO ) stock fell more than 4% on Thursday.
What's behind the move:  The AI chip and networking giant saw revenue growth amid booming AI demand, but the company's results were not enough to send the stock higher. Shares sank immediately after the results, then trimmed losses.
"I can understand the selling pressure," Cody Acree, StoneX financial equity research analyst, told Yahoo Finance. The analyst, who has a Buy rating on the stock, noted the chipmaker's fiscal Q3 revenue and earnings beat was "not enough to keep investors happy."

"The magnitude is not quite enough from a top and bottom line standpoint on the beat and raise when you have a company that is this levered to AI," said Acree.
The company's adjusted earnings per share came in at $3.32 versus Wall Street expectations of $3.23. Its quarterly revenue grew 86% year over year to $29.6 billion, topping expectations of $29.45 billion.
The company said third quarter AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion grew 221% year over year, and 54% quarter over quarter.
Broadcom said it expects revenue of $34.8 billion for its current quarter, below the $35.05 billion consensus expected by analysts, according to Bloomberg data.
( AVGO ) Go deeper with AlphaSpace

351.69 -15.55 (-4.23%)
As of 12:00:10 PM EDT. Market Open.

What else you need to know: Broadcom has seen revenue surge as tech giants race to make custom silicon and build out data centers.
"Demand for our custom AI accelerators and networking continues to be very strong," CEO Hock Tan said in the company's earnings release.
The stock is up 6% year-to-date versus peer Nvidia's ( NVDA ) 20%.

"Broadcom is really just second only to Nvidia as far as its ecosystem across the data center," said Acree. "It's just a matter of when do you enter and when do you trade around a position."
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Sebi to review CAS methodology for derivative contract settlement prices
items.author: Khushboo Tiwari
items.summary: Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is set to issue a consultation paper in a week proposing changes to the methodology used for determining settlement prices of derivative ...
items.body: Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is set to issue a consultation paper in a week proposing changes to the methodology used for determining settlement prices of derivative contracts, following feedback on the recently rolled-out Closing Auction Session (CAS) mechanism. The move comes after a major uproar from traders and other market players who cited sharp price spikes and distortions during the 20-minute CAS window, implemented from August 3. They also called out the difference between the closing price achieved through CAS and the trading prices prevailing during normal trading hours. The said distortions were higher on expiry days. Under the new mechanism, the closing price arrived at through CAS also forms the basis for settlement prices of derivative contracts on expiry. “Having considered the experience of the initial period of CAS implementation and the feedback received from various stakeholders, Sebi may be proposing certain changes in the methodology for determination of settlement prices of derivative contracts for which a consultation paper will be issued in about a week,” the regulator said in a press release on Thursday. Sebi has conducted several meetings with market participants, stock brokers, foreign portfolio investors, mutual funds and other stakeholders for feedback on the mechanism following the impact on the market during the first month of its operation. “Among the issues raised, a significant area of feedback relates to the determination of settlement prices of derivative contracts on expiry based on the closing price determined through CAS,” it added. Last month, the regulator also took action against two entities for allegedly manipulative trading during the CAS window. Apart from penalising them, the two entities were also barred from the securities market. Sebi added that the CAS framework was introduced following ‘extensive stakeholder consultations’ and detailed policy deliberations — including two rounds of public consultation between December 2025 and August 2025. “The inputs received through these consultations were carefully examined and duly considered in finalising the framework,” it noted. CAS is aimed at bringing transparency in pricing and reducing tracking error. Earlier, Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey had highlighted that the mechanism helps in catching manipulators. Following the implementation, market participants had raised concerns over low awareness and system preparedness around CAS — leaving traders confused in the initial weeks. Later, the market regulator pushed for wider participation, with brokers beginning to show indicative equilibrium prices on their systems. Following the implementation, trading volumes have come down sharply — with derivatives turnover falling to a 14-month low in August. Further, August also recorded the sharpest fall of 22 per cent in F&O turnover — the highest since December 2024. Several players had hinted at a major dent in the revenues of stock brokers on the back of falling volumes and investors turning cautious in the CAS window.

Boston College athletic director Blake James has been given a contract extension through 2031, ESPN reported Thursday.
James has been at Boston College since July 2022 after more than 11 years at Miami (Fla.), the final nine of them as athletic director.
He also was the AD at Maine from 2005-10.
He has extensive experience in NCAA circles. He is serving a four-year term as a member of the NCAA Division I Men's Ice Hockey Committee and previously served on the NCAA Board of Directors (2017-19) and the NCAA Football Oversight Committee (2015-17).
Blake also previously chaired the NCAA Division I Council, which made the day-to-day decision for Division I athletics.
He was hired to replace former AD Pat Kraft, who left the job at Boston College to become the athletic director at Penn State.

items.title: Canada invests C$4.7 billion to build VIA Rail cars domestically
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Thursday that his government will invest C$4.7 billion ($3.41 billion) to build and maintain VIA Rail passenger cars in Canada, marking the first time in four decades that the rail company's cars will be built domestically.
items.body:
Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Thursday that his government will invest C$4.7 billion ($3.41 billion) to build and maintain VIA Rail passenger cars in Canada , marking the first time in four decades that the rail company's cars will be built domestically.
"For the first time in four decades, VIA's passenger cars will be produced and assembled in Canada. Cars that used to be built in the United States will be built right here in Thunder Bay at Alstom Canada," Carney said at a news conference in Thunder Bay, Ontario.
Carney said the investment would build 313 new-generation passenger cars and support nearly 700 jobs in Ontario and Quebec.
The announcement comes amid a [USN:SPN44J009 TEXT:"worsening trade war"] with the U.S. Canadian retaliatory tariffs on about $20 billion worth of U.S. annual imports are set to come into effect on September 8, in response to tariffs levied against Canada last month by U.S. President Donald Trump , affecting $20 billion of Canadian imports.
Carney said his government was ready to sit down and strike a trade deal with the U.S. when Washington is ready, but "there must be stability and credibility" in any such agreement.
($1 = 1.3801 Canadian dollars)

Pakistan sells record $3 billion of junk debt after upgrades

The nation sold $1.75 billion of five-year debt at a yield of 7.75%, according to people familiar with the matter.

Karl Lester M. Yap

03 September, 2026 08:56 pm IST

Pakistan raised a record $3 billion from a junk bond sale after securing credit rating upgrades, taking advantage of hot debt markets.

The nation sold $1.75 billion of five-year debt at a yield of 7.75%, according to people familiar with the matter, who declined to be identified as the information is private. Pakistan also sold $1.25 billion of 10-year notes at a yield of 8.25%, the people said.

The sale attracted orders of almost $6 billion, the finance ministry said in a statement Thursday. Risk premiums offered on the debt tightened about 25 basis points during the sale process, indicating investor demand. Pakistan notes due 2031 were steady at 99.60 cents to the dollar on Thursday.

Show Full Article

Pakistan came back to the market after tapping global investors in April for the first time in more than four years in a $500 million private placement. The South Asian nation, which secured an International Monetary fund bailout in 2022 to avert a default, has been taking steps to shore up its finances and rebuild its foreign-exchange reserves.

“This will help in supporting FX reserves and will reduce reliance on risky short term dollar loans and deposit, reducing rollover risks,” said Mohammed Sohail, Chief Executive Officer at Topline Securities Ltd. in Karachi.

The sovereign’s five-year note priced broadly in line with similarly rated emerging-market government bonds sold this year. Egypt, which is rated B at S&P Global Ratings, the same as Pakistan, sold an eight-year note in May that yields around 7.7% currently, data compiled by Bloomberg show.

Rating Upgrades
Moody’s Ratings upgraded Pakistan’s sovereign credit rating last month, following in the steps of S&P, which also raised its credit score in July. The sovereign still have one of the lowest credit scores in Asia at Moody’s B3, six levels below investment grade.

“Over the past three years, Pakistan’s improving economic trajectory has increasingly been recognised through successive sovereign credit-rating upgrades and renewed access to international capital markets,” the finance ministry said in the statement. “Now global investors have reinforced that assessment with billions of dollars of actual capital.”

Bullish sentiment in credit markets in general was also supportive of the deal. Spreads on junk bonds globally are near their tightest in almost two decades as investors seek higher-coupon paying debt to protect returns against rising benchmark Treasury yields.

The average junk bond yield premiums was about 275 basis points on Wednesday, just above a 19-year low touched last week, a Bloomberg index showed.

items.title: Reform UK plans investor roadshow to build confidence in its economic approach
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Robert Jenrick, Reform UK's economy policy chief, said on Thursday he planned a roadshow to meet investors in London and New York to set out the party's economic plans and build confidence in its ability to manage Britain's public finances.
items.body:
Robert Jenrick, Reform UK's economy policy chief, said on Thursday he planned a roadshow to meet investors in London and New York to set out the party's economic plans and build confidence in its ability to manage Britain's public finances.
On the first day of Reform's annual party conference, Jenrick said he wanted to explain the anti-immigration party's plans for deep spending cuts, including cutting £50 billion from welfare spending, arguing that credibility with investors would be crucial to reducing the government's financing costs.
"The aim will be to explain, to answer questions, to listen and to instil confidence," he said. "If we come into government, we can then bring down the cost of borrowing. I don't think it will happen overnight, but I hope it will happen over a period of time as we win the trust of the markets."
Reform, led by Brexit campaigner Nigel Farage, has surged in popularity since the 2024 election, but has never run the central government, meaning it must convince investors and businesses that it is capable of governing responsibly.
British government bond yields hit their highest levels since the global financial crisis this week, adding to the challenges facing finance minister John Healey ahead of his first budget next month.

items.title: Las hermanas Mara hablan al unísono en la película de Herzog que compite en Venecia
items.author: Kristian Brunse
items.creator: Kristian Brunse
items.summary: Las hermanas Rooney y Kate Mara afirmaron que los años de experiencias compartidas les ayudaron a superar un reto interpretativo único: hablar al unísono en la película "Bucking fastard", de Werner Herzog, que se estrenó el jueves en el Festival de Cine de Venecia.
items.body:
Las hermanas Rooney y Kate Mara afirmaron que los años de experiencias compartidas les ayudaron a superar un reto interpretativo único: hablar al unísono en la película "Bucking fastard", de Werner Herzog, que se estrenó el jueves en el Festival de Cine de Venecia.
En la película, inspirada en unas gemelas británicas de la vida real, las hermanas Mara interpretan a Jean y Joan Holbrooke, cuya extraordinaria cercanía hace que hablen en perfecta sincronía, compartan los mismos sueños y se enamoren del mismo hombre. Es la primera vez que ambas actúan juntas en la gran pantalla.
"Teníamos programadas dos semanas de ensayos, pero Kate y yo nos juntamos antes porque estábamos bastante nerviosas", explicó Rooney Mara a Reuters.
No obstante, Herzog afirmó que quedó tan impresionado por lo que vio que redujo el periodo de ensayos a solo cinco días.
"Les dije: 'Ya basta. Estoy totalmente convencido de que va a quedar maravilloso. Dejen de ensayar, cállense, nos vemos en Irlanda delante de mi cámara'", explicó a Reuters. "Lo que están haciendo no tiene precedentes. No hemos visto nada parecido en la historia del cine, y dudo que volvamos a ver algo así en un futuro previsible".
Rooney Mara, conocida sobre todo por sus papeles en "La red social" y "La chica del dragón tatuado", afirmó que todo el tiempo que pasaron juntas les permitió a las hermanas desarrollar una complicidad instantánea que encajó a la perfección en cuanto empezaron a rodar.
"Había un mundo tácito entre nosotras que no nos costó nada crear. Nunca me había reído tanto; fue una experiencia única, de esas que solo se viven una vez en la vida", comentó.
Kate Mara, cuya filmografía incluye "House of Cards" y "24", afirmó que hablar sincronizadas "era casi como cantar una canción".
La película muestra cómo las dos hermanas se enamoran del mismo hombre, interpretado por Orlando Bloom. Cuando él las deja por otra mujer, tiene que solicitar una orden de alejamiento para protegerse de su furia.
Bloom dijo a Reuters que fue una experiencia increíble actuar junto a sus compañeras de reparto. "Era casi como si respiraran juntas, soñaran juntas, amaran juntas, pensaran juntas. La película parece un poema, y ellas eran el centro de atención que nos dejaba boquiabiertos", señaló.
Herzog no es ningún desconocido en Venecia. El aclamado director alemán, entre cuyas películas se encuentran "Aguirre, la cólera de Dios", "Fitzcarraldo" y "Grizzly Man2, estrenó "Grito de piedra" en el festival en 1991 y ha vuelto varias veces desde entonces tanto con largometrajes de ficción como con documentales.
"Bucking fastard" es una de las 21 películas que compiten por el León de Oro de Venecia, que se entregará el 12 de septiembre.

items.title: India's Cipla, China's Qilu partner for US launch of Merck's Keytruda biosimilar
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: India's Cipla said on Thursday its U.S. unit entered an exclusive partnership with China's Qilu Pharmaceutical to license a biosimilar version of Merck's cancer drug Keytruda for the U.S. market.
items.body:
India's Cipla (CIPL.NS) said on Thursday its U.S. unit entered an exclusive partnership with China's Qilu Pharmaceutical to license a biosimilar version of Merck's (MRK.N) cancer drug Keytruda for the U.S. market.
Here are more details:
Under the agreement, Qilu will handle development, regulatory approvals, manufacturing and supply of QL2107, a biosimilar version of Merck's Keytruda, while Cipla USA will be responsible for commercialization and sales in the United States.
QL2107 was developed to offer patients a more affordable treatment option that matches the original cancer therapy's safety and efficacy profile.
Cipla said the agreement supports its strategy to expand its oncology-focused biosimilars portfolio, leveraging Qilu's research and manufacturing capabilities and Cipla's U.S. commercial network.
Keytruda, until recently the world's top-selling drug, is used against 20 different kinds of cancerous tumors and 45 types and stages of cancer. Merck is set to lose patent protection for Keytruda in [USN:L1N44N0PO TEXT:"2028"].

items.title: Azorra vê melhora em problemas de motor e forte demanda por jatos regionais
items.author: Gabriel Araujo
items.creator: Gabriel Araujo
items.summary: A empresa de leasing de aeronaves Azorra vê sinais de que os problemas nos motores da Pratt & Whitney estão diminuindo e espera que a forte demanda por jatos menores e mais eficientes em consumo de combustível continue, apesar das turbulências no setor e dos custos mais elevados de combustível.
items.body:
A empresa de leasing de aeronaves Azorra vê sinais de que os problemas nos motores da Pratt & Whitney estão diminuindo e espera que a forte demanda por jatos menores e mais eficientes em consumo de combustível continue, apesar das turbulências no setor e dos custos mais elevados de combustível.
A Pratt & Whitney, unidade da RTX (RTX.N) , passou os últimos anos lidando com atrasos em manutenção e problemas de contaminação de metais que contribuíram para uma crise na indústria relacionada à escassez de motores e deixaram centenas de aeronaves paradas.
Os motores turbofan GTF da Pratt equipam a família E2, da Embraer (EMBJ3.SA) , e os modelos A220 e A320neo, da Airbus (AIR.PA) .
A Pratt afirmou em julho que as interrupções relacionadas à manutenção haviam diminuído e praticamente desaparecido para os modelos menores A220 e E2. No entanto, fontes da indústria disseram que a empresa ainda diverge da Airbus sobre o impacto dos problemas nos motores dos jatos maiores A320neo.
"Acreditamos que a Pratt realmente melhorou", disse à Reuters o presidente da Azorra, Ron Baur, na quarta-feira, durante um evento que marcou a entrega do 2.000º E-Jet da Embraer. "Definitivamente, vemos uma luz no fim do túnel em relação aos motores."
Baur afirmou que os problemas são comparáveis às "dores de crescimento" frequentemente observadas em novas tecnologias aeronáuticas, acrescentando que fabricantes de aeronaves e motores normalmente conseguem superar esses desafios ao longo do tempo.
CRISE ADMINISTRÁVEL As companhias aéreas globais vêm enfrentando preços mais altos dos combustíveis desde que os ataques dos Estados Unidos e de Israel ao Irã interromperam o tráfego no Estreito de Ormuz. Ainda assim, Baur afirmou que a crise é "administrável" e não enfraqueceu de forma significativa a demanda por aeronaves.
"A incerteza sempre desacelera as decisões sobre frotas, e vemos um pouco disso. Mas, na maior parte, continuamos observando uma demanda muito forte por aeronaves", disse ele, observando que as companhias aéreas têm conseguido repassar parte do aumento dos custos de combustível aos passageiros.
Ele acrescentou que a escassez global de aeronaves continua sustentando a demanda por leasing, especialmente de jatos menores, como o E2 e o A220, que transportam até cerca de 150 passageiros e consomem menos combustível do que modelos mais antigos e maiores.
A família E2 vendeu três vezes mais aeronaves do que o A220 no ano passado, embora a Airbus tenha conquistado recentemente uma grande encomenda da AirAsia. A Azorra possui compromissos de compra para ambas as famílias de aeronaves.
"Acho que ambos são aviões muito bons. Sem dúvida, a Embraer teve um ano muito forte no ano passado. Esperamos que isso continue", disse Baur.
O executivo também reiterou o interesse em uma possível versão alongada do A220, que a Airbus já estudou, mas ainda não lançou.
"Acho que uma versão alongada, o A220-500, seria muito competitiva", afirmou.
(Reportagem de Gabriel Araujo)

items.title: Fund von Werkzeug - Airbus drosselt zeitweise A330-Auslieferung
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Airbus hat die Auslieferungen seines Langstreckenflugzeugs A330neo nach dem Fund eines vergessenen Werkzeugs in einer Maschine gedrosselt. Die Ursache sei inzwischen gefunden und die Auslieferungen wieder aufgenommen worden, teilte der Flugzeugbauer am Donnerstag mit. "Wir bestätigen, dass wir kürzlich ein vereinzeltes Qualitätsproblem an einem A330-Höhenleitwerk festgestellt haben", hieß es in einer per E-Mail versandten Erklärung. Dies habe zu Inspektionen bei in der Fertigung befindlichen A330 geführt. In der Folge seien die monatlichen Auslieferungen über den Sommer verlangsamt worden. Zuerst hatte die Nachrichtenagentur Bloomberg über die Qualitätsprobleme und die Verzögerungen berichtet.
items.body:
Airbus (AIR.PA) hat die Auslieferungen seines Langstreckenflugzeugs A330neo nach dem Fund eines vergessenen Werkzeugs in einer Maschine gedrosselt. Die Ursache sei inzwischen gefunden und die Auslieferungen wieder aufgenommen worden, teilte der Flugzeugbauer am Donnerstag mit. "Wir bestätigen, dass wir kürzlich ein vereinzeltes Qualitätsproblem an einem A330-Höhenleitwerk festgestellt haben", hieß es in einer per E-Mail versandten Erklärung. Dies habe zu Inspektionen bei in der Fertigung befindlichen A330 geführt. In der Folge seien die monatlichen Auslieferungen über den Sommer verlangsamt worden. Zuerst hatte die Nachrichtenagentur Bloomberg über die Qualitätsprobleme und die Verzögerungen berichtet.
Im Juni und Juli lieferte Airbus keine A330-Maschine aus. Im August wurde dann eine A330 dem Kunden übergeben. Insgesamt lieferte der Konzern in dem Monat 57 Flugzeuge aus, wie aus Airbus-Daten hervorgehen dürfte, die kommende Woche veröffentlicht werden sollen. Einer mit der Angelegenheit vertrauten Person zufolge wurde das Werkzeug bei einer Inspektion vor der Auslieferung im Inneren der Flugzeugstruktur entdeckt.
Das Höhenleitwerk, das die Neigung der Flugzeugnase steuert, wird in den spanischen Airbus-Werken hergestellt. Der Fund stehe nicht im Zusammenhang mit den jüngsten Streiks in den spanischen Werken, sagte die Person weiter. Das Risiko von Schäden durch Fremdkörper (Foreign Object Damage, FOD) ist in der Luftfahrtindustrie ein bekanntes Problem. Dazu können bei der Produktion oder Wartung vergessene Gegenstände wie Werkzeuge oder auch Lappen gehören.

items.title: Everest adventure becomes story of loss in Venice festival documentary
items.author: Crispian Balmer
items.creator: Crispian Balmer
items.summary: A documentary about two elite mountaineers pursuing an apparently impossible dream became a study of grief and resilience after tragedy struck during production, its directors said at the Venice Film Festival on Thursday.
items.body:
A documentary about two elite mountaineers pursuing an apparently impossible dream became a study of grief and resilience after tragedy struck during production, its directors said at the [USN:L8N4422FV TEXT:"Venice Film Festival"] on Thursday.
"Everest: The Other Side" began as the story of ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson and their ambition to climb and ski down Everest's direct North Face, a forbidding route few climbers have ever completed and no one has skied.
But the National Geographic documentary took a catastrophic turn after Nelson died in 2022 while skiing down Nepal's Mount Manaslu -- a scene captured on film.
"It started as a love story between Jim and Hilaree and their dreams of climbing and skiing the Direct North Face. We never could have anticipated the tragedy that ensued," co-director Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi told reporters.
UNPRECEDENTED MOUNTAIN VIEWS The film follows Morrison as he confronts the loss of his partner and decides whether to continue their dream alone.
His journey is given added pathos by the fact his life was already scarred by tragedy, with his wife and their two young children dying in a 2011 plane crash.
"For me, the film really looks at this question through Jim's eyes of how you can move through grief," Vasarhelyi said. "How do you learn to live with grief? How does that grief inform a life of intention?"
Morrison said the mountains that had shaped his life also helped him cope with repeated personal losses.
"I've suffered a lot of loss in my life and the mountains have provided a lot back to me," he said. "My craft is putting one foot in front of another and taking one day at a time."
The film is directed by Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin, the Oscar-winning duo behind the climbing documentary "Free Solo".
Chin, who accompanied Morrison on the Everest mission, said the new project sought not only to capture an unprecedented mountaineering feat but also the emotional and practical decisions made in one of Earth's most hostile environments.
"No one's ever seen mountaineering like this," Vasarhelyi said, referring to footage shot on Everest's remote North Face.
Chin described the challenge of filming an expedition where climbers and camera operators were operating at nearly 9,000 metres (29,500 ft).
"The team was made up of world-class athletes and climbers who could also shoot," he said. "You have to be climbers first."
The directors also highlighted the role of the Sherpa climbers who formed part of the expedition team, saying a new generation was increasingly pursuing its own ambitions rather than simply supporting Western expeditions.
For Chin, however, the film's deeper message lies beyond mountaineering.
"When you face your mortality on a fairly regular basis, it is about looking at your life through the lens of the inevitable," he said. "It can shape the way that you decide to live."
The film is being shown out of competition at the Venice Film Festival, which runs until September 12.

items.title: US to seek back payment from Europe for Ukraine aid, Trump says
items.author: The Straits Times
items.summary: WASHINGTON, Sept 3 - U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday said he would ask European nations to pay back the United States for military aid and munitions previously sent to Ukraine and appeared to signal a halt in sales to allied nations.
items.body:
US to seek back payment from Europe for Ukraine aid, Trump says
Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox

U.S. President Donald Trump speaks while hosting a dinner in the Rose Garden at the White House in Washington, D.C., U.S., September 2, 2026. REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein

Published   Sep 03, 2026, 11:21 PM

Updated   Sep 03, 2026, 11:21 PM

Set as preferred source

WASHINGTON, Sept 3 - U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday said he would ask European nations to pay back the United States for military aid and munitions previously sent to Ukraine and appeared to signal a halt in sales to allied nations.
In a social media post, Trump also slammed reports of heavily depleted U.S. munition stockpiles amid the separate war in Iran, while adding that the United States was stockpiling munitions.
"We are taking them for ourselves, the U.S.A., rather than selling them to others, but the sales to Allies will soon again, begin," Trump wrote.

"Hundreds of Billions of Dollars was given to Ukraine and NATO, free of charge, that Europe would have paid for — If they were only asked, but we will be asking for that money, though somewhat belatedly!" he added.
Reuters reported last month that the U.S. Army has used up much of its stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles during the Iran war, raising concerns about the military's readiness for future conflicts. REUTERS

items.title: Monedas suben por debilidad del dólar tras comentarios de Waller de la Fed
items.author: Manuel Farías
items.creator: Manuel Farías
items.summary: Las principales monedas de América Latina subían el jueves, en un escenario de retroceso del dólar en los mercados internacionales, que era presionado por comentarios del gobernador de la Reserva Federal Christopher Waller, que dijo que podría respaldar el mantener las tasas de interés si los datos confirman que la presión sobre los precios se está moderando.
items.body:
Las principales monedas de América Latina subían el jueves, en un escenario de retroceso del dólar en los mercados internacionales, que era presionado por comentarios del gobernador de la Reserva Federal Christopher Waller, que dijo que podría respaldar el mantener las tasas de interés si los datos confirman que la presión sobre los precios se está moderando.
* Waller dijo el jueves que se inclina por mantener la paciencia en materia de política de tasas de interés, mientras observa si las presiones sobre los precios se moderan.
* "Voy a parafrasear aquí a John Lennon: 'Démosle una oportunidad a la desinflación' y esperemos una reunión para ver cómo se presentan los datos", dijo Waller en un evento de Reuters NEXT en Washington.
* Sus comentarios golpeaban al dólar ante sus principales cruces, lo que era amplificado, además, por la nueva fuerte alza del yen ante apuestas de alzas de tasas por parte del Banco de Japón.
* A nivel de datos en Estados Unidos, el número de personas que solicitaron prestaciones por desempleo aumentó de forma leve la semana pasada, el crecimiento de la productividad laboral se aceleró en el segundo trimestre, el déficit comercial se amplió de forma considerable en julio y la actividad del sector servicios de Estados Unidos repuntó en agosto.
* Los inversores, en tanto, aguardan los datos de nóminas no agrícolas de agosto -que se publicarán el viernes- para analizar el posible próximo movimiento en materia de tasas de interés por parte de la Fed en su reunión de mediados de septiembre.
* El peso mexicano intentaba una recuperación, tras perder más temprano más de un 0,2%. y subía un 0,01%, a 16,9618 unidades por dólar; en tanto que el índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , integrado por las 35 acciones más líquidas del mercado, trepaba un 0,98%, a 65.520,26 puntos, apuntalado principalmente por las acciones de firmas mineras ante el alza de los precios de los metales.
* El real brasileño perdía un 0,22%, a 5,1022 por dólar, luego de avanzar con fuerza en la sesión previa, al tiempo que el referencial bursátil Bovespa (.BVSP) ganaba un 0,72%, a 186.530 puntos, ampliando sus avances tras dispararse en la víspera.
* El peso colombiano se fortalecía un 0,49%, a 3.143,50 unidades por dólar, en su tercera jornada de apreciación, en tanto que el índice accionario de la bolsa, el MSCI COLCAP (.COLCAP) repuntaba un 0,96%, a 2.513,19 puntos.
* El peso chileno , subía un 0,43%, a 934,50/934,80 unidades por dólar, impulsado por el retroceso global del billete verde y un avance en los precios del cobre, la mayor exportación del país. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) cedía un 0,27%, a 11.525,19 puntos.
* El peso mayorista argentino mostraba una leve mejora del 0,13% a 1.509 unidades por dólar, con el banco central (BCRA) interviniendo a diaria a favor de reforzar sus reservas internacionales. El índice líder S&P Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires retrocedía un 0,28%.
* La moneda peruana, el sol , se apreciaba un 0,12%, a 3,3590/3,3600 unidades por dólar. Por su parte, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) avanzaba apenas un 0,08%, a 1.573,62 puntos.
items.raw_description: Las principales monedas de América Latina subían el jueves, en un escenario de retroceso del dólar en los mercados internacionales, que era presionado por comentarios del gobernador de la Reserva Federal Christopher Waller, que dijo que podría respaldar el mantener las tasas de interés si los datos confirman que la presión sobre los precios se está moderando.

items.title: US to seek back payment from Europe for Ukraine aid, Trump says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday said he would ask European nations to pay back the United States for military aid and munitions previously sent to Ukraine and appeared to signal a halt in sales to allied nations.
items.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday said he would ask European nations to pay back the United States for military aid and munitions previously sent to Ukraine and appeared to signal a halt in sales to allied nations.
In a social media post, Trump also slammed reports of heavily depleted U.S. munition stockpiles amid the separate war in Iran, while adding that the United States was stockpiling munitions.
"We are taking them for ourselves, the U.S.A., rather than selling them to others, but the sales to Allies will soon again, begin," Trump wrote.
"Hundreds of Billions of Dollars was given to Ukraine and NATO, free of charge, that Europe would have paid for — If they were only asked, but we will be asking for that money, though somewhat belatedly!" he added.
Reuters [USN:L1N43W1IH TEXT:"reported last month"] that the U.S. Army has used up much of its stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles during the Iran war, raising concerns about the military's readiness for future conflicts.

items.title: Bundesregierung: Halten an Personalabbau 2027 fest - Aber mehr Stellen bei Sicherheitsbehörden
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Die Bundesregierung hat einen Bericht der "Bild" zurückgewiesen, nach dem der Bund von seinem im Koalitionsvertrag vereinbarten Personalabbauziel abrückt. Im Gegenteil werde die Bundesregierung auch 2027 das Personal in Bundeseinrichtungen um zwei Prozent reduzieren, sagte ein Regierungssprecher der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters auf Anfrage. Davon seien aber ausdrücklich die Sicherheitsbehörden ausgenommen. Dort gibt es einen gewünschten Aufwuchs bei Bundeswehr, Zoll oder Bundespolizei um mehrere tausend Personen.
items.body:
Die Bundesregierung hat einen Bericht der "Bild" zurückgewiesen, nach dem der Bund von seinem im Koalitionsvertrag vereinbarten Personalabbauziel abrückt. Im Gegenteil werde die Bundesregierung auch 2027 das Personal in Bundeseinrichtungen um zwei Prozent reduzieren, sagte ein Regierungssprecher der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters auf Anfrage. Davon seien aber ausdrücklich die Sicherheitsbehörden ausgenommen. Dort gibt es einen gewünschten Aufwuchs bei Bundeswehr, Zoll oder Bundespolizei um mehrere tausend Personen.
Tatsächlich steht im schwarz-roten Koalitionsvertrag das Ziel: "Stellenabbau in der Bundesverwaltung um acht Prozent (zwei Prozent/Jahr) (Ausnahme für Sicherheitsbehörden)". Die "Bild" bezieht sich auf eine Studie der "Initiative Neue Soziale Marktwirtschaft"(INSM), in der es heißt, dass der Bund die Zahl der Stellen 2027 um 12.347 erhöhen wolle.
"Die Zahl ist nicht aktuell und zudem irreführend, wenn sie in den Zusammenhang mit dem Einsparziel von acht Prozent gesetzt wird", sagte der Regierungssprecher. Dieses Ziel sei bewusst nicht für die sicherheitsrelevanten Planstellen gesetzt worden. "Der eigentliche Abbaupfad zu der vereinbarten Stelleneinsparung von acht Prozent sieht wie folgt aus: 2025 wurden 0,5 Prozent Personalabbau vereinbart und umgesetzt. Für 2026 wurde das Ziel von ursprünglich vereinbarten zwei Prozent auf 2,2 Prozent erhöht. Für 2027 und 2028 sind zwei Prozent und für 2029 1,5 Prozent vorgegeben."
Die genauen Zahlen ließen sich zudem erst nennen, wenn das Haushaltsgesetz 2026 verabschiedet sei. Erst dann könnten die aktuellsten Daten berücksichtigt werden. Der Personalabbau im Bund zählt zu den zentralen Versprechen der Regierung neben dem Bürokratieabbau. Zugleich soll aber etwa die Bundeswehr um mehrere tausend Soldaten aufgestockt werden.

items.title: En el valle de Nepal, devastado por las inundaciones, no queda nada en pie
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Desde el aire, el tramo del valle del río Trishuli, en Nepal, donde los equipos de rescate intentan llegar hasta los cientos de trabajadores atrapados en centrales hidroeléctricas, se presenta como una extensión gris y totalmente desolada.
items.body:
Desde el aire, el tramo del valle del río Trishuli, en Nepal, donde los equipos de rescate intentan llegar hasta los cientos de trabajadores atrapados en centrales hidroeléctricas, se presenta como una extensión gris y totalmente desolada.
Ocho días después del catastrófico alud, el suelo se ha endurecido como el hormigón o se ha convertido en una masa húmeda y resbaladiza, y no se vislumbra ningún indicio de asentamiento humano en amplias extensiones.
Al llegar en helicóptero, el fotógrafo de Reuters Navesh Chitrakar vio cómo unas excavadoras intentaban retirar enormes rocas de la boca de un túnel en la central hidroeléctrica Upper Trishuli 3A. Sin embargo, la abertura era tan pequeña que los equipos de rescate nepalíes solo podían intentar entrar en el túnel arrastrándose por dentro.
Las autoridades estiman que unas 900 personas se encuentran atrapadas en el interior de seis centrales hidroeléctricas de este pequeño país del Himalaya, donde el derrumbe de un glaciar el pasado miércoles provocó una gigantesca ola de lodo, rocas y agua que arrasó los valles montañosos, causando la muerte de más de 1.200 personas.
Otros trabajadores de Upper Trishuli 3A estaban drenando el agua del interior del túnel y preparándose para llevar a cabo voladuras controladas perforando las enormes rocas, de modo que las excavadoras pudieran adentrarse más en el interior.
Pueblos como Syabrubesi, que en su día fue una puerta de entrada a las rutas de senderismo del Himalaya salpicada de casas, aparecían ahora como una capa de barro grisáceo, de la que solo quedaban unos pocos edificios.
No había signos visibles de vida en este escenario apocalíptico, señaló Chitrakar, y las marcas en las imponentes montañas a ambos lados del río Trishuli sugerían que las aguas de la crecida podrían haber subido hasta 500 metros por encima de los niveles normales.
En el paso fronterizo de Gyirong, donde las imágenes de vigilancia mostraban a personas intentando huir segundos antes de que un alud de lodo engullera el cruce entre China y Nepal, se podía ver a algunos rescatistas con uniformes rojos junto con maquinaria pesada.
Pero no quedaba nada en pie, según el fotógrafo de Reuters. Ni edificios, ni puerta, ni puente.

items.title: Hamilton comienza su fin de semana en Monza con estilo y dejando huella
items.author: Alan Baldwin
items.creator: Alan Baldwin
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton comenzó con fuerza su fin de semana del Gran Premio de Italia al presentarse en Monza por todo lo alto, al volante de su propio Ferrari F40, un coche de ensueño que, de niño, nunca pensó que llegaría a conducir.
items.body:
Lewis Hamilton comenzó con fuerza su fin de semana del Gran Premio de Italia al presentarse en Monza por todo lo alto, al volante de su propio Ferrari F40, un coche de ensueño que, de niño, nunca pensó que llegaría a conducir.
Desafiando el calor sofocante —se había declarado alerta por calor en el ultrarrápido e histórico "Templo de la Velocidad"—, el siete veces campeón del mundo de Fórmula Uno llegó el jueves con un elegante traje negro y posó para los fotógrafos con un grueso abrigo de color beige.
Este look recordaba a su llegada a un Maranello lluvioso en enero del año pasado, cuando posó junto a un F40 con un impecable traje negro y abrigo.
Hamilton, cinco veces ganador en Monza con McLaren y Mercedes, declaró a los periodistas que es "la mejor sensación" ser piloto de Ferrari en la carrera de casa de este glamuroso equipo y que quería estar a la altura de las circunstancias y destacar la historia.
El piloto de 41 años, cuyo equipo celebra además el 30º aniversario de la primera victoria de Michael Schumacher en el Gran Premio de Italia, explicó que llevaba tiempo buscando un F40 —un auto que Ferrari fabricó entre 1987 y 1993, del que se vendieron unas 1.300 unidades— que tuviera una historia interesante y un bajo kilometraje.
Encontró uno que había sido conducido desde la fábrica de Maranello hasta la casa de su propietario, a 69 kilómetros de distancia, y que nunca más se volvió a poner en marcha. La puerta del copiloto permaneció sin abrirse y el bólido cubierto con una lona protectora.
Pero aún le esperaban más sorpresas al piloto que compite con el número 44.
"Lo que también fue una locura es que, cuando desmontaron el auto para revisarlo, lo primero que vieron fue que había resistido el paso del tiempo. Todo seguía funcionando. Apenas hubo que cambiar nada", comentó.
"Y cuando sacaron el motor, descubrieron que llevaba el número 44. El número 44 estaba grabado en el motor. No me lo podía creer", agregó.
Si eso fue el destino, Hamilton esperará que vuelva a sonreírle en Monza, donde intentará recortar distancias con el líder del campeonato mundial de F1, Kimi Antonelli.
Ferrari cuenta con una mejora del motor, mientras que el piloto de Mercedes comenzará la carrera desde la parte trasera de la parrilla debido a sanciones relacionadas con el motor.
"Todo ayuda; todo ayuda", afirmó Hamilton, que está empatado a puntos con el segundo clasificado, George Russell, 59 puntos por debajo del italiano.
El británico, que contará con la presencia de su madre este fin de semana en uno de los circuitos más emblemáticos y apasionantes de este deporte, afirmó que Ferrari cuenta ahora con una "estrella polar" —una orientación clara hacia donde deben llegar— de la que carecía la temporada pasada.
"Ver cómo cada fin de semana llegan nuevas piezas que mejoran el auto es emocionante; demuestra que estamos avanzando. Sigo creyendo firmemente que tenemos lo que hace falta para ganar", añadió.
"La presión es alta. Quieres dar lo mejor de ti por el equipo. Está toda esa gente que trabaja en la fábrica y muchos de ellos vendrán a esta carrera", indicó. "Los tifosi acuden en masa, su pasión es inigualable, y también quieres dar lo mejor de ti para ellos".

items.title: Wall Street avanza con el alivio en los bonos y nuevas señales de cautela desde la Fed
items.author: Carlos Rodríguez Salcedo
items.summary: Los comentarios de Christopher Waller moderan la presión sobre los bonos, mientras el mercado espera el informe de empleo del viernes.
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — Las acciones estadounidenses abren al alza este jueves, mientras el descenso de los rendimientos de los bonos alivia parte de la presión sobre Wall Street. El mercado recibe con optimismo las declaraciones del gobernador de la Reserva Federal, Christopher Waller, aunque el petróleo mantiene en foco los riesgos de inflación. Ver más: De la firma a la ejecución: los desafíos que enfrenta el plan petrolero de EE.UU. en Venezuela El S&P 500 gana 0,44%, mientras el Dow Jones Industrial suma 0,66%. El Nasdaq Composite sube 0,44%. El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 años cae cinco puntos básicos, a 4,73%, después de acercarse a 4,8% ante el repunte de los precios de la energía y las apuestas a que la Fed podría retomar las alzas de tasas. Waller dijo que estaría dispuesto a mantener la tasa de referencia sin cambios en la reunión del 15 y 16 de septiembre si la inflación continúa su avance hacia la meta de 2%. Sin embargo, dejó abierta la puerta a un endurecimiento monetario si las presiones sobre los precios vuelven a acelerarse. “Si hay un progreso continuo hacia nuestro objetivo de 2%, estoy dispuesto a apoyar que la tasa de política se mantenga en su nivel actual”, afirmó Waller. “Pero si la inflación resulta elevada, consideraría un aumento de tasas”. La atención ahora se concentra en el informe oficial de empleo del viernes. Los economistas estiman que las nóminas aumentaron en 55.000 puestos en agosto, después de la inesperada caída del empleo en julio. Waller espera que las cifras confirmen que el mercado laboral permanece en un estado satisfactorio. La trayectoria de los bonos conserva un papel central para las acciones. Emmanuel Cau, jefe de estrategia de renta variable europea de Barclays, afirmó que “es muy difícil ver al mercado de acciones subir sin algún grado de estabilización en el mercado de bonos” y consideró que existe espacio para “reducir beta de forma selectiva”. Cau señaló que una inflación y unas nóminas más débiles podrían permitir nuevos avances de las acciones. En cambio, datos superiores a lo previsto elevarían el nerviosismo. El estratega advirtió que el mercado se ha vuelto mucho más sensible a la volatilidad de las tasas y que un rendimiento del Tesoro a 10 años de 5% aumentaría la presión. → Suscríbete al newsletter Línea de Mercado , una selección de Bloomberg Línea con las noticias bursátiles más destacadas del día. Los elevados rendimientos también comenzaron a atraer compradores hacia la deuda soberana. Harvey Bradley, jefe de inversión global en tasas de Insight Investment, dijo que los bonos gubernamentales ofrecen valor y anticipó menores rendimientos durante los próximos 12 meses. El petróleo, no obstante, mantiene vivo el riesgo inflacionario. El Brent sube 0,9%, a US$96,49 por barril, después de acumular un avance superior a 8% en las tres sesiones anteriores. El WTI gana 1,4%, a US$92,30, ante nuevas hostilidades entre Estados Unidos e Irán y el riesgo de una mayor participación de Israel. Irán afirmó que atacó bases estadounidenses en Kuwait y Emiratos Árabes Unidos, mientras Israel advirtió que podría ampliar su respuesta. La tensión volvió a colocar al estrecho de Ormuz en el centro de la atención por su importancia para los flujos globales de crudo. Donald Trump aseguró que unos 18 millones de barriles diarios pasan por el estrecho, apenas por debajo de los niveles previos a la guerra. Empresas que rastrean los flujos marítimos calculan volúmenes mucho menores. Operadores estimaban recientemente un tránsito de entre 6 millones y 8 millones de barriles diarios. En Estados Unidos, los inventarios de crudo cayeron casi 4,5 millones de barriles la semana pasada, su primer descenso desde finales de julio. Las existencias en Cushing, Oklahoma, subieron de forma marginal, a 22,5 millones de barriles. El oro avanza por segunda sesión consecutiva ante la debilidad del dólar y la incertidumbre geopolítica. El metal sube 1,1%, a US$4.428,89 por onza. La plata gana 0,6%, a US$65,69, mientras platino y paladio también registran avances. Ver más: Kalshi da el salto al español tras el Mundial y ubica la expansión internacional como prioridad En el mercado cambiario, el yen llegó a apreciarse 1,8%, hasta 155,85 unidades por dólar, ante mayores apuestas por un alza de tasas del Banco de Japón y el temor a otra intervención oficial. Japón gastó un récord de US$96.400 millones durante el último mes para respaldar su moneda. El Banco de Japón se inclina por elevar este mes su tasa de referencia en 25 puntos básicos, desde el actual 1%, según personas familiarizadas con el asunto citadas por Bloomberg . La decisión se conocerá el 18 de septiembre y podría representar el intervalo más corto entre dos aumentos desde que Kazuo Ueda asumió como gobernador. El bitcoin ( XBTUSD ), por su parte, cotizaba cerca de US$77.900 y no logró consolidar una ruptura sobre US$80.000. La demanda de inversores estadounidenses mostró señales irregulares, pese a una mejora de los flujos hacia los fondos cotizados de bitcoin al contado durante agosto. Así se han comportado los precios del bitcoin. Símbolo: XBTUSD:CUR. Clase de activo: crypto. La apertura deja así a Wall Street entre dos fuerzas. Las señales de moderación de la inflación y el retroceso de los rendimientos ofrecen respaldo a las acciones, mientras el petróleo y la guerra mantienen abierta la posibilidad de nuevas presiones sobre los precios y las tasas. El dólar opera a la baja esta mañana, aunque ING mantiene una visión favorable para la moneda estadounidense. Francesco Pesole, estratega de divisas del banco neerlandés, considera que las tasas de corto plazo y los mayores precios de la energía siguen apuntando a un fortalecimiento del billete verde. La atención del mercado se concentra ahora en los datos de EE.UU. ING considera que el umbral para que las cifras económicas aparten a la Reserva Federal de una subida de tasas en septiembre es elevado. BBVA, por su parte, destacó señales mixtas en la economía y coincidió en que el foco estará en el reporte laboral y la inflación. En medio de este contexto, las monedas de América Latina tienen un desempeño mixto. El peso chileno ( USDCLP ), el colombiano ( USDCOP ) y el argentino ( USDARS ) avanzan, mientras caen el real brasileño ( USDBRL ) y el peso mexicano ( USDMXN ). BBVA señaló que el apetito por los activos de mercados emergentes continúa respaldado por la estabilidad de las bolsas globales. Sin embargo, el banco destacó una divergencia significativa entre las monedas de la región, con el real brasileño liderando las ganancias y las divisas andinas rezagadas. - Victoria’s Secret ( VSXY ) se desploma pese a elevar su previsión anual de ventas a entre US$7.100 millones y US$7.180 millones. Las ventas comparables crecieron 9% en el segundo trimestre, pero la desaceleración decepcionó tras el avance de 57% que acumulaban las acciones este año. - Nvidia ( NVDA ) acordó comprar Hugging Face por unos US$13.000 millones, su mayor apuesta para ampliar su ecosistema de IA. La operación le dará control sobre una plataforma clave para compartir modelos y datos, que seguirá abierta a desarrolladores y otros fabricantes de chips. Hugging Face fue valorada en US$4.500 millones hace tres años. Así se han comportado las acciones de Victoria's Secret. Símbolo: VSXY:UN. Clase de activo: equity. - Airbus detectó problemas de calidad en el estabilizador horizontal del A330neo, lo que frenó casi por completo sus entregas entre junio y agosto. La compañía aseguró que identificó la causa y reanudó las entregas. Airbus acumula unos 475 aviones entregados este año, cerca de 400 menos que su objetivo anual. - Blue Origin, de Jeff Bezos, contrató al menos a 47 exempleados del proyecto satelital Amazon ( AMZN ) Leo durante el último año para impulsar TeraWave, su futura red de miles de satélites. El servicio estará enfocado en empresas y gobiernos y prevé comenzar a desplegar satélites a finales de 2027.

items.title: USA Lutnick s'excuse pour avoir dit qu'aucun Américain n'est mort pendant la guerre contre l'Iran
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le secrétaire américain au Commerce, Howard Lutnick, a présenté jeudi ses excuses pour avoir déclaré à la télévision qu'aucun soldat américain n'avait été tué depuis le début de la guerre contre l'Iran, disant avoir fait une confusion avec l'opération militaire américaine au Venezuela.
items.body:
Le secrétaire américain au Commerce, Howard Lutnick, a présenté jeudi ses excuses pour avoir déclaré à la télévision qu'aucun soldat américain n'avait été tué depuis le début de la guerre contre l'Iran, disant avoir fait une confusion avec l'opération militaire américaine au Venezuela.
"Je me suis mal exprimé. Dix-huit membres de nos forces armées ont perdu la vie, et je suis profondément attristé pour ces familles ; je leur présente mes sincères condoléances. Je pensais à l'opération militaire au Venezuela, au cours de laquelle aucun militaire n'a perdu la vie", a dit Howard Lutnick dans un message publié sur X.
Le secrétaire au Commerce a tenu ces propos mercredi lors d'une interview accordée à la chaîne CNBC, au cours de laquelle il n'a pas été question du Venezuela.
Evoquant la gestion par Donald Trump de "la situation avec l'Iran", Howard Lutnick s'est dit convaincu que la stratégie d'étranglement économique allait être "très efficace", après s'être félicité qu'il n'y ait "pas eu de victimes américaines" dans ce conflit.

items.title: Malte Tensions après l'acquittement du commanditaire présumé de l'assassinat d'une journaliste
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le gouvernement maltais a appelé au calme après l'acquittement d'un homme d'affaires accusé d'avoir commandité l'assassinat, en 2017, de la journaliste d'investigation Daphne Caruana Galizia.
items.body:
Le gouvernement maltais a appelé au calme après l'acquittement d'un homme d'affaires accusé d'avoir commandité l'assassinat, en 2017, de la journaliste d'investigation Daphne Caruana Galizia.
La journaliste et militante anti-corruption, âgée de 53 ans, a été tuée dans un attentat à la voiture piégée devant son domicile en octobre 2017. Son assassinat a déclenché une tempête politique à Malte et braqué les projecteurs sur la police et le système judiciaire de l'île.
Le verdict rendu mercredi soir à l'issue du procès du commanditaire présumé a provoqué la colère de la famille de la victime et d'une partie de la classe politique, et suscité les critiques de l'organisation Reporters sans frontières (RSF), qui s'est dite "plus qu'indignée" de "l'absence de justice pleine et entière près d'une décennie après le crime".
Roberta Metsola, présidente du Parlement européen et ancienne responsable politique maltaise, s'est engagée à tout faire pour que justice soit rendue. "Nous n'abandonnerons pas et nous ne céderons pas", a-t-elle promis.
Dans un communiqué, le gouvernement maltais a lancé un appel "à la prudence dans les déclarations publiques qui pourraient faire plus de mal que de bien".
À l'issue de précédents procès, trois hommes avaient été condamnés à de lourdes peines de prison pour avoir commis l'assassinat et deux autres pour avoir fourni la bombe.
En revanche, l'homme d'affaires Yorgen Fenech, héritier d'un empire immobilier comprenant notamment des hôtels et des casinos, a été acquitté mercredi par un vote du jury à huit voix contre une des chefs d'accusation de complicité et d'association de malfaiteurs en vue de commettre un assassinat.
La journaliste, est-il noté dans l'acte d'accusation, était sur le point de publier un article compromettant sur l'un des proches de Fenech avant d'être assassinée.
Le parquet ne peut pas faire appel du verdict, sauf dans des circonstances exceptionnelles liées à des points de droit.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Vladimir Soldatkin

［ウラジオストク（ロシア）　３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Vladimir Soldatkin

［ウラジオストク（ロシア）　３日　ロイター］ - ロシアのプーチン大統領は３日、拡大傾向が顕著になっている財政赤字について、ロシア経済の「深刻な」リスクにはならず、管理は可能との認識を示した。極東ウラジオストクで開催されている国際経済会議「東方経済フォーラム」で「ロシアの債務は世界で最も低い水準にあり、深刻な問題には当たらない」と発言した。

ロシアの２０２６年１─７月の財政赤字は前年同期比４０％拡大。財政赤字の国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比は２．８％と、２６年の公式目標である１．６％を大きく上回っている。

約４年半に及ぶウクライナとの戦闘に要する費用は増大している。２５年は経済が減速し、政府は増税や債務の拡大を余儀なくされている。ウクライナはロシア領内の製油所や民間倉庫に対するドローン（無人機）攻撃を強化。ロシアは燃料不足に陥り、インフレの加速や中小企業の疲弊が目立っている。

ロシア中央銀行は今月１１日に理事会を開催する。企業側は経済を成長軌道に戻すため、現在１４．００％の政策金利を１２％未満に引き下げるよう求めている。ロイターが今週まとめた調査によると、アナリストらは政策金利の据え置きを見込んでいる。

プーチン氏は、経済が冷え込み過ぎないことは重要だとする一方で、現在の金融政策は過度に引き締められていないと主張。政府が企業支援のための複数の融資プログラムを策定していると言及した。

items.title: Bank of England's Pill says higher rates would help head off inflation pressure
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said that raising interest rates now would help reduce the chance that the central bank has to be more aggressive in future to tame inflation which has picked up as a result of the Iran war.
items.body:
Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said that raising interest rates now would help reduce the chance that the central bank has to be more aggressive in future to tame inflation which has picked up as a result of the Iran war.
"Raising Bank Rate ... need not be the start of a prolonged and aggressive series of increases," Pill said in comments that he was due to deliver to the Edinburgh Chamber of Commerce later on Thursday.
"Implemented and communicated effectively, a prompt increase in Bank Rate may serve to head-off some of the potential insidious 'catch up' nominal dynamics that threaten to make temporary departures of inflation from target more persistent," he added.
Pill and two other Monetary Policy Committee members voted to raise interest rates in July. But they were outvoted by colleagues who preferred no change as they awaited clearer signs of what the Iran war means for long-term inflation pressures.
Investors in interest rate futures on Thursday priced the chance of a quarter-point rate hike at the MPC's next meeting this month at little more than 15% although that probability rose to more than 70% for the subsequent meeting in November.
items.raw_description: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said that raising interest rates now would help reduce the chance that the central bank has to be more aggressive in future to tame inflation which has picked up as a result of the Iran war.

items.title: Boeing predicts Africa aircraft fleet will more than double by 2045
items.author: Vincent Nzilani
items.creator: Vincent Nzilani
items.summary: Africa's commercial aircraft fleet will more than double by 2045, U.S. planemaker Boeing forecast on Thursday, as a young and increasingly urban population drives demand for travel within the continent and to the Middle East.
items.body:
Africa's commercial aircraft fleet will more than double by 2045, U.S. planemaker Boeing (BA.N) forecast on Thursday, as a young and increasingly urban population drives demand for travel within the continent and to the Middle East.
The following are further points from its annual Commercial Market Outlook.
Africa's fleet will grow to 1,625 aircraft in 2045 from 755 in 2025, requiring 1,165 airplane deliveries over the next two decades.
Single-aisle aircraft, used mainly on domestic and regional routes, will account for 870 of the forecast deliveries, or about three-quarters of the total.
Boeing expects deliveries of 240 wide-body jets, which are typically used on longer international routes, and 15 cargo planes.
Passenger traffic within Africa is expected to grow 6.5% annually through 2045.
Africa-Middle East traffic would expand 7.1% a year, the fastest rate among the region's major travel markets.
Traffic between Africa and Europe is projected to grow 3.4% annually.
The region's cargo fleet is expected to rise to 150 freighters from 60, supported by growth in logistics, e-commerce and exports.
Carriers including Ethiopian Airlines, EgyptAir and Kenya Airways (KQNA.NR) , whose fleets mainly consist of Boeing and Airbus (AIR.PA) jets for long-haul routes, dominate the African market.
Boeing's Managing Director Commercial Marketing Africa and Middle East Shahab Matin said Africa's market was "entering a period of sustained growth driven by improving connectivity, expanding intraregional travel and deeper economic ties".
Africa's dominant carriers typically use Embraer (EMBJ3.SA) , ATR and De Havilland planes on regional routes.
But Matin said Boeing could also provide appropriate carriers.
Boeing also estimated that Africa's aviation services market, including maintenance, repair, overhaul, modifications and digital services, would be worth $140 billion over the 2026-2045 period.
Meeting the expansion will require 75,000 additional aviation workers, including 22,000 pilots, 25,000 technicians and 28,000 cabin crew, Boeing said.
The forecast is a long-term market outlook rather than an order projection.
items.raw_description: Africa's commercial aircraft fleet will more than double by 2045, U.S. planemaker Boeing forecast on Thursday, as a young and increasingly urban population drives demand for travel within the continent and to the Middle East.
